pr.reading: No ROC-derived threshold is applied to a PR-AUC contrast, and no practical-importance label is attached to one. The frozen D29 text asks only for C1, C2 and C3 "read again with average precision (and the trapezoid PR-AUC the release reports)" and defines no PR-AUC margin; the first version of this reader reused the ROC rule strings (D18 |mean| > 3 with 4 of 5 units agreeing; the E30 C2/C3 "within 3" / "> 3 above LP" cuts; the D29 noise rule's "mean > 3") and the margin-3 TOST. That compared one fixed 3-point margin against AP baselines from 1.5 to 44 points and hid measured differences: Siena BIOT raw head AP 1.65 -> 2.20, +0.55 [+0.14, +0.96], about +33% relative, was labelled "no difference shown" because 0.55 < 3. Those labels and the margin-3 TOST are withdrawn here (change made 2026-11-05, AFTER the results, in answer to an external review; post hoc). Each PR-AUC contrast now reports the two arm means, the absolute difference with its 95% t-interval over the stated units, the relative change in percent of the baseline arm, and whether the interval excludes 0 - which is the only inference claim made. A relative change on a near-zero baseline is unstable, so the baseline is printed next to every percentage and should be read with it. No PR-AUC margin is defined in its place: defining one now, after seeing the data, would be a post hoc threshold, and the prevalence-scaled alternatives already in the artifacts (AP / prevalence, scripts/analysis/coverage.py and handcrafted_baseline.py) are reported there rather than turned into a cut here. Every ROC reading in these files is unchanged.
